module_doc:
H1 test: GradCuit-style test-time latent steering in the concept stream of a trained v2 core (frozen weights).

Latents = offsets dz on the concept-stream inputs X at the 2 positions just before the query (SEP, Q), i.e. between the
'prompt' (facts) and the 'continuation' (the chain answers). Update exactly as GradCuit: loss = -R * sum_t log p(pred_t)
over the model's own greedy continuation, R = -1 if the verifier rejects the final answer, Adam, <= 10 updates, stop when correct.
Baselines at the same verifier budget (11 calls): random-direction steering, sampling (BoN), rank enumeration; and extra passes.

definitions.name: ZCRMSNorm
definitions.doc: Zero-centred RMSNorm: (1 + gamma) * x / rms(x); gamma starts at 0 and IS weight-decayed (Qwen3.8).

definitions.name: ShortConv
definitions.doc:
Causal depthwise conv, kernel 4, dilation 1, residual form x + sum_i w_i * x_{t-i}.
w starts at 0 (exact identity at init). Document-aware: never mixes across segment boundaries.

definitions.name: GRRead
definitions.doc: x = mean_i g_i * zcRMS(R_i), g_i = sigmoid(U_i V_i rms(R_i) + b_i); rank 32, b_i = +2 (gate ~0.88).

definitions.name: GRWrite
definitions.doc: s_i = 2 sigmoid(u_i^T x + a_i); u and a start at 0, so s_i = 1 exactly at init.

definitions.name: Attn
definitions.doc: Gated attention. SWA: window 8, partial RoPE (16/64). FULL: NoPE + learnable per-head temperature (no WD).

definitions.name: Layer
definitions.doc: 'S': both sublayers read {L}, write {L,G}.  'F': both sublayers (attention AND FFN) read {L,G}, write {G} only.

definitions.name: Engram
definitions.doc:
Orders {2,3}, 4 hash heads each, prime-row tables x 48 dims; context gate; conv k=4 dilation 1.
Keys use canonical token ids (case + leading-space merged, built offline) and reset at document starts.

Task (synthetic, V=512, T=256, one document per row):
  [BOS P P P] [F k v S]x4 facts | ~204 tokens of local Markov filler | 4 queries: [Q k P P][P P P v]

  python e2e.py --test                      pipeline unit tests (float64, exact)
  python e2e.py --arm confined --steps N    train one arm on the long-range recall task (harness.py task)
Arms: confined (proposed, D0 = tok + P) | stack (NCP-style control) | confined_read (rejected arm);
--nextlat adds the NextLat auxiliary.  --task single | multi (--n_facts 1 = the 3-token carry task).
Task: 4 facts [F k v S] at the start, ~204 tokens of Markov filler, 4 queries [Q k P P][P P P v]; every answer is
>= 200 tokens after its fact, far beyond the token-path reach (70 confined / 83 stack), so it can only come through
the concept core.  Chance on answers = 1/32.

module_doc:
Deterministic task generators for the HRM-CC vs Nanbeige-loop experiment (generator version v1).

Every generator: gen(rng, split) -> Example(segments=[(text, scored, label), ...], family, meta).
Documents are the concatenation of segment texts; scored segments are the evaluated answer spans
(teacher-forced greedy exact match == all scored tokens argmax-correct). Training uses dense NTP on
every token of every document (both models identically).

Splits: 'train', 'val', 'test' share the in-distribution (ID) structural ranges and differ only by seed.
'ood' uses held-out structure: longer chains / deeper hops, larger graphs, unseen identifier alphabet,
unseen operator combinations, unseen permutation sizes, longer distances.
Verify the compat shim: (1) forward bit-identical to the original in float64; (2) run hrm_encoder.mps_smoke_test.

  python train.py --run_dir ../runs/main --hours 48 --milestone_hours 24

Per optimizer step: K ~ U{8..12} core passes (same K for every micro-batch of the step), windows of 4 (remainder merged

LR: warm-up (steps) then cosine to lr_min_frac * lr over the TRAINING-TIME bud

definitions.doc: Follow a chain of pointers h hops. ID: 8-16 pointers, hops 1-4. OOD: 20-28 pointers, hops 5-8.

definitions.name: gen_graph_walk
definitions.doc: Labeled directed graph; follow a sequence of edge labels. ID nodes<=8, walk<=4; OOD nodes 10-16, walk 5-7.

definitions.name: gen_state_machine
definitions.doc: Finite-state program over input symbols. ID states<=5, input len 2-6; OOD states 7-9, input 8-12.

definitions.name: gen_permutation
definitions.doc: Apply a permutation r times to a list. ID size 3-5, r 1-3; OOD size 6-7 (unseen family), r 1-3.

definitions.name: gen_variable_binding
definitions.doc: Chains of assignments with copies and +/- constants. ID chain 1-4; OOD chain 5-8 or unseen names.

definitions.name: gen_variable_binding_newnames
definitions.doc: OOD-only: same as variable_binding (ID depth range) but with the unseen identifier alphabet B.

definitions.name: gen_kv_updates
definitions.doc: set/get over a key-value store with overwrites. ID ops 4-12; OOD ops 20-30.

definitions.name: gen_relational
definitions.doc: Family-tree composition: 'X is the parent of Y'. Query the h-th descendant. ID h 1-3; OOD h 4-6.

definitions.name: gen_arith_transform
definitions.doc:
start value then a sequence of ops mod 100. ID: 1-4 ops, 'mul' never directly after 'sub'.
OOD: 3-6 ops, always containing the held-out pair 'sub' then 'mul' (unseen operator combination).
Eval buckets OOD by meta.depth: 3-4 ops isolates th

definitions.name: gen_stack_ops
definitions.doc: push/pop sequence; answer = popped values in order then final stack. ID ops 3-10; OOD ops 14-20.

definitions.name: gen_nested_scopes
definitions.doc: Nested blocks with shadowing; each print shows the innermost binding. ID nesting 1-3; OOD 4-6.

definitions.name: gen_brackets
definitions.doc: Complete an unbalanced bracket prefix. ID open depth 1-6; OOD depth 8-12.

definitions.name: gen_seq_transform
definitions.doc: reverse / sort / dedupe a list of numbers. ID length 3-8; OOD length 12-16.

definitions.name: gen_kv_retrieval
definitions.doc:
Many key: value pairs, then query one key. Distance (in pairs) between the queried pair and the
query is recorded. ID pairs 4-24; OOD (longer context) pairs 40-60.

definitions.name: gen_copy
definitions.doc: Copy a random string after a filler gap. The gap (filler sentences) controls distance.

definitions.name: gen_needle
definitions.doc: A code inserted into filler prose; asked at the end. Needle depth (sentences after needle) varies.

definitions.name: gen_json_lookup
definitions.doc: Nested JSON object; query a key path. ID depth 1-2; OOD depth 3-4.

definitions.name: gen_py_exec
definitions.doc: Tiny Python function + call; answer = printed value. ID 1-3 statements; OOD 4-6 statements.

definitions.name: gen_json_build
definitions.doc: Emit a JSON object from a key=value description (syntactic exactness).

definitions.name: gen_yaml_like
definitions.doc: YAML-like config; query a nested field (identifier copy through structure).

definitions.name: gen_sort_trace
definitions.doc: Algorithm trace: bubble-sort passes over a small list (each pass is an answer step).

definitions.name: gen_expr_eval
definitions.doc: Evaluate a nested arithmetic expression (mod 100). ID nesting 1-2; OOD 3-4.

definitions.name: gen_tool_traj

Deterministic simulated tools. GOAL -> CALL -> OBS -> ... -> ANSWER. Every CALL and the ANSWER are
scored segments (next-action accuracy, final-state accuracy). With p=0.2 an injected error observation
appears after the first call; the corr

Read-only companion probe: kernel spectrum of single adaptation episodes.

The V10.2 protocol (§6.3) commits three support examples per episode. A write
changes that episode's replayed corrections by -eta*K_episode*G, so the
finite-step amplification is lambda_max of the episode's own code-partitioned
Gram matrix. This samples 3-document episodes from the same frozen V10.1
checkpoint and dev panel as the companion probes. Output refuses to overwrite.

Read-only companion probe: spectrum of the code-partitioned RBF kernel.

Uses the same frozen V10.1 checkpoint and the same 64/64/32/32 dev panel as
probe_v10_1_interfaces.py (seed 20261012). For each family and sigma it builds
the kernel Gram matrix of all panel queries within each code partition and
reports its largest eigenvalue. A gradient write with step eta changes the
replayed corrections by -eta*K*G, so finite-step stability scales with
eta*lambda_max(K). Output refuses to overwrite.

module_doc:
Read-only companion to probe_latent_baselines.py: why is the raw PQ forecast
worse than a linear map of itself?

Two mechanisms predict different things. If the soft-PQ convex combination
shrinks the forecast toward the codebook centroid, var(F2)/var(target) is small
and a per-coordinate affine fit (scale and shift only) recovers most of the
ridge gain. If F lives in a rotated subspace, the affine fit does not help and
only a full linear map does. Same checkpoint, panels and seeds as the baseline
probe; step 61,384 only. Output refuses to overwrite.

module_doc:
Read-only probe: can Local-Support-Learning GMM gates separate data
distributions inside the frozen V10.1 model?

LSL (Ben-Kish et al., 2026) gates a low-rank adapter per weight matrix with
  open(x) = log Phi_pos(x) > log Phi_neg(x)
where Phi_pos is a diagonal GMM fitted on the new phase's inputs to that matrix
and Phi_neg on a small generic reference sample. The paper reports results on
1.5B-7B models and notes that retention depends on representation quality. This
probe measures the gate at width 128.

Sites are the inputs of attention (qkv) and FFN (up) matrices:
  e2.<i>.attn / e2.<i>.ffn   Reader output of two-stream block i, per visit
  core.<i>.attn / .ffn       RMSNorm output inside concept block i, per visit
  dec.<i>.attn / .ffn        RMSNorm output inside decoder block i
Proto

Read-only probe: do GMM gates separate phases within one data family?

probe_gmm_gates.py treated whole families (text, math, Sudoku) as phases. A
realistic continual-learning phase is narrower. Here each of the four math
modules is a phase. For each held-out module, Phi_pos is fitted on half of its
documents and Phi_neg on a reference covering everything else the model trained
on (the other three modules, text and both Sudoku families). Reported: hit rate
on the module's held-out documents and open rate on the other modules' held-out
documents, raw per row (no smoothing; see the companion probe). Sites: E2 and
concept-core attention/FFN inputs, per visit, plus decoder inputs. Reuses the
companion's GMM settings. Dev split, frozen checkpoint; output refuses to overwrite.

module_doc:
Read-only probe: does V10.1's concept forecast beat trivial baselines?

The training "latent" loss is the MSE between the PQ forecast of group g and the
stopped, online pooled E3 state of group g+1. Its absolute value can rise while
prediction improves, because the target's spread changes during training. This
probe scores the forecast against baselines on the same targets:

  mean        per-coordinate mean of targets from a disjoint calibration draw
  persistence predict P3[g+1] by P3[g]
  ridge(P3)   linear map P3[g] -> P3[g+1], fitted on the calibration draw
  ridge(U2)   linear map from the final concept state U[g] -> P3[g+1]
  ridge(F2)   linear map from the PQ forecast F[g] -> P3[g+1]

and reports every MSE divided by the target variance on the scored panel
(fraction of variance une

Read-only probe: what does the second concept visit add, and would the
decoder gain anything from the visit-1 state or the change between visits?

For the frozen step-61,384 checkpoint, per family:
  relative change   RMS(U2 - U1) / RMS(U2) over valid groups
  cosine            mean cosine similarity of U1 and U2 per slot
  predictive value  FVU of ridge readouts of the next pooled state P3[g+1]
                    from U1, U2, the delta U2 - U1, and [U1, U2] concatenated,

Same panels and seeds as probe_latent_baselines.py. Dev split, no training;

module_doc:
Objectives for the tiny arms.

C0  token CE only.
A   v10_1.model.losses unchanged (latent MSE, codeword fitting, chunk head,
    hard-argmin exploration with selector CE).
X   token CE + 0.1 * forecast-only future CE on the committed codes (V10.2)
    + 0.1 * mixture likelihood on candidate updates (V10.3):

      ll_k  = -sum_j mask_j * CE_{k,j}           visit-2 forecast of code k
      log_pi = log_softmax(selector[rows, at])    prefix-only prior
      L_mix = -mean_doc( logsumexp_k(log_pi_k + ll_k) / n_doc )

    Every one of the K branches carries gradient, weighted by its posterior
    responsibility; the selector is trained as the mixture prior rather than by
    cross-entropy on a hard winner. This is the smooth (maximum-likelihood)
    form of best-of-K training in Explorative Mo

Formulas (per block, width d):

module_doc:
Internal RL (ETA paper §"Internal reinforcement learning", C.5, Algorithms 1–3) and the raw-action RL baseline.

Internal RL: the frozen base, the frozen metacontroller switch unit and controller decoder are the environment.
A causal policy pi(z | e_{1:t}) (1-layer GRU, Gaussian with learned log-std) replaces the acausal encoder. At
each decision unit the frozen switch emits beta (thresholded at 0.5; the first unit always switches); only at
switches is a new z sampled, otherwise z is held, so the policy acts on the abstract timescale. Sparse reward:
1 if the whole task is completed. Advantage = (R - mean) / (std + 1e-3) over the batch (critic-free, C.5.2).
Objective: PPO-clip on log pi(z) of the switch decisions (2 epochs per batch).

Raw-action RL baseline: the same estimator on the base'

action (pair index) the environment currently requires *when that row was appended* — i.e. the subgoal of the
next action — which ground-truth controllers use as their label (paper C.3), and which a group-rate controller
reads at the group's release row.

judge='task'  : success iff the given task is completed (post-training evaluation; sparse reward).
judge='any'   : success iff the visited colour sequence completes *some* pretraining task, failure as soon as it
                is not a prefix of any (base competence on its own pretraining distribution).

Train HRM THINKER v2 (19M). One process, one device; resumable; pause-aware; 48 h in ONE schedule (v1 lesson D-041).

  python train.py --run_dir ../runs/main --hours 48 --milestone_hours 24
  python train.py --run_dir ../runs/main --resume ../runs/main/ckpt_last.pt

Per optimizer step: K ~ U{8..12} core passes (same K for every micro-batch of the step), windows of 4 (remainder merged
into the last), carry detached between windows, per-window backward (c_hat and tok are leaves whose gradients accumulate;
one backward into the encoder at the end of the micro-batch).
Loss = NTP + 0.1 * mean_r NCP(u_r) + 0.1 * consistency(final window) + VQ + 0.01 LB + 0.001 z
       + lambda_h * NextLat-h + lambda_KL * NextLat-KL.
LR: warm-up (steps) then cosine to lr_min_frac * lr over the TRAINING-TIME bud

definitions.name: ShortConv

definitions.name: GRRead

definitions.name: GRWrite

definitions.name: Engram

definitions.doc: Follow a chain of pointers h hops. ID: 8-16 pointers, hops 1-4. OOD: 20-28 pointers, hops 5-8.

definitions.name: gen_graph_walk
definitions.doc: Labeled directed graph; follow a sequence of edge labels. ID nodes<=8, walk<=4; OOD nodes 10-16, walk 5-7.

definitions.name: gen_state_machine
definitions.doc: Finite-state program over input symbols. ID states<=5, input len 2-6; OOD states 7-9, input 8-12.

definitions.name: gen_permutation
definitions.doc: Apply a permutation r times to a list. ID size 3-5, r 1-3; OOD size 6-7 (unseen family), r 1-3.

definitions.name: gen_variable_binding
definitions.doc: Chains of assignments with copies and +/- constants. ID chain 1-4; OOD chain 5-8 or unseen names.

definitions.name: gen_variable_binding_newnames
definitions.doc: OOD-only: same as variable_binding (ID depth range) but with the unseen identifier alphabet B.

definitions.name: gen_kv_updates
definitions.doc: set/get over a key-value store with overwrites. ID ops 4-12; OOD ops 20-30.

definitions.name: gen_relational
definitions.doc: Family-tree composition: 'X is the parent of Y'. Query the h-th descendant. ID h 1-3; OOD h 4-6.

definitions.name: gen_arith_transform
definitions.doc:
start value then a sequence of ops mod 100. ID: 1-4 ops, 'mul' never directly after 'sub'.
OOD: 3-6 ops, always containing the held-out pair 'sub' then 'mul' (unseen operator combination).
Eval buckets OOD by meta.depth: 3-4 ops isolates th

definitions.name: gen_stack_ops
definitions.doc: push/pop sequence; answer = popped values in order then final stack. ID ops 3-10; OOD ops 14-20.

definitions.name: gen_nested_scopes
definitions.doc: Nested blocks with shadowing; each print shows the innermost binding. ID nesting 1-3; OOD 4-6.

definitions.name: gen_brackets
definitions.doc: Complete an unbalanced bracket prefix. ID open depth 1-6; OOD depth 8-12.

definitions.name: gen_seq_transform
definitions.doc: reverse / sort / dedupe a list of numbers. ID length 3-8; OOD length 12-16.

definitions.name: gen_kv_retrieval
definitions.doc:
Many key: value pairs, then query one key. Distance (in pairs) between the queried pair and the
query is recorded. ID pairs 4-24; OOD (longer context) pairs 40-60.

definitions.name: gen_copy
definitions.doc: Copy a random string after a filler gap. The gap (filler sentences) controls distance.

definitions.name: gen_needle
definitions.doc: A code inserted into filler prose; asked at the end. Needle depth (sentences after needle) varies.

definitions.name: gen_json_lookup
definitions.doc: Nested JSON object; query a key path. ID depth 1-2; OOD depth 3-4.

definitions.name: gen_py_exec
definitions.doc: Tiny Python function + call; answer = printed value. ID 1-3 statements; OOD 4-6 statements.

definitions.name: gen_json_build
definitions.doc: Emit a JSON object from a key=value description (syntactic exactness).

definitions.name: gen_yaml_like
definitions.doc: YAML-like config; query a nested field (identifier copy through structure).

definitions.name: gen_sort_trace
definitions.doc: Algorithm trace: bubble-sort passes over a small list (each pass is an answer step).

definitions.name: gen_expr_eval
definitions.doc: Evaluate a nested arithmetic expression (mod 100). ID nesting 1-2; OOD 3-4.

module_doc:
Exploratory oracle controllability, not RL or deployable latent reasoning.

Frozen weights, real legal prefixes, zero offsets, 10 steps, three registered
learning rates. Compare C input, intermediate S1 and output u. Optimise the
probability of the expert optimal-action set; compare random projected offsets
with the oracle run's per-example step norms. All prompts run the full budget,
so both corrections and damage to initially correct predictions are measured.

Change a relevant layout fact while keeping the entire action history valid.

At the first pair-second decision, swap the target odd colour's location with
another unvisited colour. Require disjoint optimal next-action sets. This tests
whether the prediction follows the changed fact, rather than merely the prefix.
No task/subgoal label is fed to the model.

k-token padding, one doc id per item, every item starting on a k boundary.

Run-folder compatibility shim (the reference files stay byte-identical; see DECISIONS.md D-001).

hrm_encoder.EncoderLayer defines a helper named `_apply(L, G, y, s)`, which shadows torch.nn.Module._apply(fn).
Module.to(device) / .float() / .double() call child._apply(fn), so moving any model that contains an EncoderLayer
raises TypeError. This shim renames the helper to `_write_streams` and rebinds forward to it. The arithmetic is
unchanged token for token (verified bit-exact against the original forward in float64, see runs/tests/).

Stand-in for the concept module (v2 as tested in the concept test bench, K = 1, i.e. without the XM latent).

ONE shared layer looped R times: reads {X, S}, writes S; X = c_hat (re-read every pass, gradient flows), S0 = 0;
R ~ U{1..4} in training.  Layer = the encoder's FULL layer at concept rate (gated attention, NoPE + per-head

NCP: product-quantised vocabulary (k-means++ init, dead-code restarts, trained by L_VQ only), distance head,
cross-entropy on the next concept's code indices.  c_pred = sum_n pi_n sg(e_n).
Only its interface matters for the decoder: (u, c_pred) per chunk, post-loop.

module_doc:
HRM THINKER - Decoder v1 (design candidate).  Reference implementation + exact unit tests.

What the decoder receives (and nothing else):
  tok      (B, T, d)   encoder token stream = zcRMSNorm(L), reach 63
  u        (B, M, dc)  concept-core output state per chunk (post-loop only)
  c_pred   (B, M, dc)  NCP prediction of the NEXT chunk, made at each chunk
  doc      (B, T)      document ids
  E        (V, d)      the encoder's embedding matrix (tied output head)

Plan (target-aligned concept shift): position t predicts x_{t+1}; it reads chunk j*(t) = floor((t+1)/4) - 1, the newest
chunk whose last token 4j*+3 <= t.  P_t = W_u u_{j*} + W_c c_pred_{j*} + o_{r(t)}; r(t) = (t+1) mod 4 is the index of
x_{t+1} inside its chunk.  A learned null plan replaces W_u u + W_c c when j* < 0 or chunk j*

definitions.name: ZCRMSNorm
definitions.doc: y = (1 + gamma) * x / rms(x); gamma initialised to 0 and weight-decayed.

definitions.name: ShortConv
definitions.doc:
Causal depthwise conv, kernel K, dilation 1, residual form:
  y_t = x_t + sum_{i=0}^{K-1} w_i * x_{t-i}       (w initialised to 0 -> identity)
Document-aware: x_{t-i} from another document contributes 0.

definitions.name: GRRead
definitions.doc:
Gated-residual read over the allowed streams:
n_i = rms(R_i),  g_i = sigmoid(U_i V_i n_i + b_i),  x = mean_i g_i * (1+gamma_i) * n_i

definitions.name: GRWrite
definitions.doc: Per-stream write scale s_i = 2 * sigmoid(u_i . x + a_i); u, a initialised to 0 -> s_i = 1.

module_doc:
HRM THINKER - Encoder v1.0 (frozen).  Reference implementation.

Two role streams:
  L  (local)  : bounded reach (63 tokens at window 8). Only stream the decoder may read.
  G  (global) : includes FULL-attention writes. Read only by the CRC -> concept core.
Layer pattern "SSSFSSSF", Engram after layer index 0 (S1).

Inputs  (all int64, shape (B, T), T % chunk == 0):
  ids        token ids
  doc        document id per position (packing); positions of different docs never interact
  eng_idx    (B, T, n_tables) Engram row indices, precomputed with `engram_indices` (CPU is fine)
Outputs:
  tok        (B, T, d)        normalised L stream  -> decoder token path
  c_hat      (B, M, d_c)      concepts on the sphere radius sqrt(d_c), M = T / chunk -> concept core
  aux        dict(L, G, mix)  for t

HRM Thinker v4 (draft_v4.md, revision 2), size-parametric: FULL = 19,898,011 compute parameters at k = 6; TINY for
the CPU experiment in v4_tiny/.

Encoder (§3): v3's 8 layers SSSFSSSF (F layers 6 heads), L/G gated residual, ONE Engram gather feeding read 1 (after
  layer 0, with conv) and read 2 (after layer 4); NEW: F layers 3 and 7 applied twice in place (enc_loop = 2); NEW:
  shared SwiGLU beside every layer's own FFN, y = FFN_l(x) + g_l * FFN_shared(x) (g_l = 1, shared W2 = 0);
  NEW: pooler over k tokens (§3.5.4): 4-head attention (W_V = W_O = I, q = b = p = 0) then a SwiGLU on the pooled vector
  (W2 = 0, g = 1); pads masked; an empty chunk falls back to uniform weights. "linear" = v3's pool (ablation).

module_doc:
Gridworld-pinpad (Kobayashi et al. 2025, arXiv 2512.20605, Appendix A.1), tokenised for the v4-vs-LLM tiny experiment.

Environment (paper A.1.1-A.1.2): G x G grid (G = 7), O = 8 uniquely coloured cells, W = 4 walls, episode limit 100 steps.
4 actions (N, E, S, W); moving into a wall or off the grid is a no-op. A coloured cell is visited when the agent moves
onto it from a different cell. Visiting the wrong colour ends the episode (failure); visiting all task colours in order
is success. Colours, walls and the start cell are sampled without overlap at the start of every episode.
Tasks: the 16 pretraining tasks of Table A1 (compositions of the abstract subgoals 0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7); held-out = the
other 20 three-pair compositions without a repeated consecutive pair; long = the post-training

module_doc:
Long-range probe families (PROMPT 4.4). Every item puts its evidence at least FLOOR tokens before the answer
(FLOOR = 128 > 90 required; chosen above the S2 stack decoder's reach of 103, DECISIONS D-011).

Documents are assembled from pre-encoded token segments, so a name or value has exactly the same tokens in the fact
and in the answer (each segment is encoded once, with its leading space, and reused). Distances are measured in
tokens on the assembled document and asserted.

Item = dict(ids, spans=[(start, end, label)], family, meta, dist) with ids ending in EOS; spans index the answer tokens
(the prediction for token i is logits[i-1]).

Throughput shims with identical arithmetic (V-006).

The encoder's ShortConv recomputes `same_doc_shift_mask(doc, i)` (pad + compare) for every conv and every shift:
3 shifts x 3 convs x 8 layers + Engram = 75 boolean masks per forward, all from the same `doc`. Inside one
Encoder.forward the masks depend only on (doc, i), so they are memoised for the duration of that call. The masks carry
no gradient, so the backward pass is unaffected. The memo is THREAD-LOCAL: the data-prefetch thread also calls
same_doc_shift_mask (engram_indices) concurrently and always takes the original path.

module_doc:
Phase D: discover persistent latent actions over the frozen transplanted system, then internal RL over Z.

Stage 1 (discovery, ETA-style metacontroller [R5] adapted to our Z pathway):
  switch    beta_m = sigmoid(MLP([e_m ; Z_{m-1}]))                  causal
  proposal  Zt_m ~ q_D(. | demonstration)  (bidirectional GRU over [e_m ; c_{m+1}])   training only
  Z_m = (1 - beta_m) Z_{m-1} + beta_m Zt_m ;  forced beta=1 at the first walk boundary (chunk 30)
  loss = walk NLL through the frozen core (prior guidance) + decoder
         + lam_D * sum_m KL(q_D(Zt_m) || p_ref(Zt_m | e_m))   (p_ref = Phase B prior; ungated, per review §7.3)
Stage 2 (RL): Gaussian policy pi(Z | e_m, Z_prev) = prior mean + learned residual (zero-init), switch = frozen
  hardened beta (kappa=0.5) from stage 1; REINFORCE

S6 Local Support Learning, scaled configuration (draft §10.1, §10.4, §10.6).

LSL-scaled: rank-16 LoRA on q, k, v, o, w12, w3 of every gated block; one gate for q/k/v (block input n1(x)),
one each for o, w12 and w3 on that matrix's own input; JL projection 64; Phi_pos 16 / Phi_neg 32 diagonal GMMs;

Execution is full recomputation (no caches), so smoothing state is exact per sequence.

module_doc:
S5 methods and budgets (draft §9.5-§9.6, I17).

Budgets are multiples b of one greedy answer's wall-clock t_g, measured on the same batch (lockstep over a batch of
items, so every method batches across items like greedy decoding). Search methods size their expansions per search
adaptively from the measured time per expansion so that the expected wall-clock meets the budget; a hard stop at 2x
the budget marks unfinished items as failures ('wall_clock'); overruns are reported.
Methods: rh (RH(H), decoder-free), rh_grounded (mechanism comparison), g (one-tree G(R), G(1) grounded; IMAG = R None),
token_tree (3 colours + STOP, code-free prior, grounded children), best_of_n (T = 1 code-free sampling), greedy.
Fit the token tree's value head on S4's executed trajectories with the chosen token decoder (§9.6).

module_doc:
V9 queue watchdog.

Every 15 minutes it checks the block drivers (Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, QF) and keeps the queue moving:

  * a driver that died (crash, SIGKILL, reboot) while its block is running or waiting is relaunched with code/launch_block.py,
    which refuses unless the block's lock and its contract and smoke tests still match; a block whose training child is still
    alive is never relaunched (that would start a second copy of the same run);
  * a block whose status is 'failed' is resumed the same way, at most MAX_ATTEMPTS times per stage with RETRY_GAP between tries,
    then it is left alone and an alert is raised (a deterministic failure would otherwise loop forever);
  * a block that was stopped on purpose ('stopped_by_user', i.e. the driver received SIGTERM or SIGINT) is NOT res

Inline src/ into one self-contained page: index.html (opens from disk, or served by serve.py) and v9_atlas.html (artifact body, no skeleton).

    python build.py [--no-snapshot]

The page reads live telemetry from serve.py when it is reachable. Without a server it falls back to a labelled snapshot of the
experiment's files taken at build time (window.V9_SNAPSHOT), so a page opened from disk or published elsewhere still shows
real numbers, stamped with when they were taken.

Build the V9 Guide.

  ../v9_guide.html  the same body in a full page, for opening from disk or serving locally
Chapter files are src/ch_*.html (sorted), widgets src/viz_*.js (sorted), the 3D module src/three_guide.js.
variants.js is read from ../src (the Atlas descriptor table) so an arm is defined once for both pages.

module_doc:
V9 Atlas telemetry server (read-only, loopback only).

    python serve.py [--port 8765]

Serves the built page at / and one JSON endpoint, /api/telemetry, aggregated from the experiment's own files under
v9_tiny/. Nothing is written, no path comes from the request, and every source is a fixed pattern:

    runs/status*.json  runs/launch_*.json  runs/driver*.json  runs/G1.json  runs/queue.jsonl
    runs/<run>/log.jsonl  runs/<run>/config.json  runs/<run>/development_step_*.json  runs/<run>/train_summary.json
    runs/<run>/measure.json (greedy rates only)  runs/<run>_dev/summary.json  runs/<run>_trained_contracts/summary.json
    tests/q*_contracts.json  tests/q*_smoke.json     spec/LOCK_*.json
